'''Argüman''' is a [[free and open source software]] for collective [[structured argumentation]] and argument analysis via argumentation graphs or [[argument map]]s in which the type of connections can be specified.<ref name="CollectiveDebate">{{cite thesis |last1=Yuan |first1=An |title=Collective debate |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/122893 |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |access-date=13 June 2023 |date=2018|hdl=1721.1/122893 |type=Thesis |pages=19–22}}</ref><ref name="10.1007/978-3-319-61660-5_23">{{cite book |last1=Pührer |first1=Jörg |title=Logic Programming and Nonmonotonic Reasoning |chapter=ArgueApply: A Mobile App for Argumentation |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |date=2017 |volume=10377 |pages=250–262 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-61660-5_23 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-61659-9 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="RankingSemantics">{{cite web |title=Argumentation Ranking Semantics based on Propagation |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316856422 |access-date=13 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gargouri |first1=Anis |last2=Konieczny |first2=Sébastien |last3=Marquis |first3=Pierre |last4=Vesic |first4=Srdjan |title=On a Notion of Monotonic Support for Bipolar Argumentation Frameworks |journal=Proceedings of the 20th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and MultiAgent Systems |date=3 May 2021 |pages=546–554 |publisher=International Foundation for Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems|url=https://hal.science/hal-03225627/ |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |title=Socratrees: Exploring the Design of Argument Technology for Layman Users |eprint=1812.04478 |last1=Jeuris |first1=Steven |year=2018 |class=cs.HC |page=5}}</ref> It allows users to create collaborative "semantic maps" of arguments in well structured [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]] formats and share them with an audience and potential participants.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Antonio |first2=Cordón|last2= García|first1= José |title=Lectura, sociedad y redes: Colaboración, visibilidad y recomendación en el ecosistema del libro |date=1 January 2018 |publisher=Marcial Pons |isbn=978-84-9123-626-9 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BPrVDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA129 |page=129 |language=es}}</ref><ref name="10.1007/978-3-319-61660-5_23"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Argüman – About |url=https://en.arguman.org/about|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124053021/https://en.arguman.org/about |archive-date=2021-01-24 }}</ref> Arguman.org was an open structured social debate platform that implemented the software.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Benetos |first1=Kalliopi |chapter=Digital Tools for Written Argumentation |title=Digital Writing Technologies in Higher Education |journal=Digital Writing Technologies in Higher Education: Theory, Research, and Practice |date=2023 |pages=81–99 |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-36033-6_6 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |language=en|doi-access=free|isbn=978-3-031-36032-9 }}</ref> It is down as of 2023. There also is a mobile version of the tool. The project was started, in 2014, and largely built by developers in Turkey.<ref name="fosdem"/>

[[File:Gource visualization video of Argüman development, an argument map software (sped-up).webm|thumb|[[Gource]] visualization video of the development of Argüman.]]
Some studies used or investigated excerpts of argumentations on the platform.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Gradual Semantics Accounting for Similarity between Arguments |url=https://cdn.aaai.org/ocs/18077/18077-78629-1-PB.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the Sixteenth International Conference on Principles of Knowledge Representation and Reasoning |pages=1–2}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hoffmann |first1=Michael H. G. |title=The Elusive Notion of "Argument Quality" |journal=Argumentation |date=1 June 2018 |volume=32 |issue=2 |pages=213–240 |doi=10.1007/s10503-017-9442-x |s2cid=254261703 |language=en |issn=1572-8374}}</ref> Unlike the larger and functional alternative [[Kialo]], which is structured using only 'Pro' and 'Con' relations,<ref name="CollectiveDebate"/> argüman arguments are structured by three types of premises – 'because', 'but', and 'however'.<ref name="10.1007/978-3-319-61660-5_23"/> As of the latest version, debates are presented in their entirety as a large tree which may be harder to navigate than other formats – for instance, trees "can become extremely dense, and the interface does not make it obvious which arguments the user should pay attention to".<ref name="CollectiveDebate"/> Users can also flag arguments for [[fallacies]]. Arguman.org also had a Turkish-language subdomain.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Uzelgun |first1=Mehmet Ali |last2=Kucukural |first2=Onder |last3=Oruc |first3=Raluni |title=Four Approaches in Argumentation Analysis |url=https://run.unl.pt/handle/10362/116025 |website=Connectist: Istanbul University Journal of Communication Sciences |access-date=9 September 2023 |pages=265–297 |doi=10.26650/CONNECTIST2020-0666 |date=2020|s2cid=243065887 |doi-access=free |hdl=10362/116025 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

A researcher{{Who|date=July 2024}} suggested the concept of the [[Semantic Web]]-interoperability could be useful for argumentative structures on the Web, going beyond the conventional flat structures of discussions and lack of characterizations of their components as implemented in argüman.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Vetere |first1=Guido |title=L'impossibile necessità delle piattaforme sociali decentralizzate |journal=DigitCult - Scientific Journal on Digital Cultures |date=30 June 2018 |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=41–50 |doi=10.4399/97888255159096}}</ref> There is research into how to automatically use these collaborative argumentation graphs, which is a "very active" topic in [[Artificial intelligence|Artificial Intelligence]].<ref name="RankingSemantics"/> There also is research into applying conclusion-making methods to the debates or their data, such as bipolar weighted argumentation frameworks – this could be a way to find out what the current conclusion of debates like "[[Computer Science]] is not actually [[Branches of science|a science]]" is.<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Delobelle |first1=Jérôme |title=Ranking-based Semantics for Abstract Argumentation |date=12 December 2017 |url=https://hal.science/tel-01937279/ |publisher=Université d'Artois |type=phdthesis |language=en}}</ref> A study suggests it could be useful for the development of critical thinking skills.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bir Eleştirel Düşünme Çevrimiçi Aracı Olarak Arguman.org |url=https://inet-tr.org.tr/inetconf20/bildiri/62.pdf |access-date=9 September 2023}}</ref>
